prompt: `first.py` rendered two interfaces with Jinja2's defaults. How many blank lines did its output have?
`{% if i.description is ___ %}` asks whether the key exists at all.
What does `trim_blocks=True` remove?

choices.text: The spaces and tabs before a block tag
The first newline after a block tag
Every blank line in the output, including those written on purpose
Comments

prompt: Why does a stray blank line in a rendered configuration matter, if the router ignores it?

choices.text: FRR refuses a configuration file with a blank line anywhere in it, and keeps the old one
It is a difference in every diff, hiding the ones that mean something
Each blank line makes rendering slower, and a large network renders thousands of them
YAML cannot hold it

prompt: A colleague writes `{%- if ... -%}` on every tag instead of setting the two options. What is the case against it?
hint: What happens at the next edit?

choices.text: Jinja2 does not support `{%-`
It also removes the values that sit between the tags, not only the whitespace
It trims by hand, and the next tag somebody adds will lack it
It renders more slowly, because every tag is trimmed separately while rendering

The value of `adress`, matched by spelling

prompt: Why is an empty value worse than an exception, for a router configuration?

choices.text: It takes longer to render
It cannot be committed to Git
The file looks complete, so nothing stops it being sent
Exceptions are logged by the router

prompt: With `StrictUndefined` on, how does the template say that an interface may have no description?
hint: The decision is written where a reader can see it.

choices.text: It cannot: every value has to be present in the data
By wrapping the line in `{% if i.description %}`
By turning `StrictUndefined` off for that interface
choices.why: It is set for the whole environment.

choices.text: By writing `description:` with no value in the YAML of every router
choices.why: That puts the decision in every file instead of one.
